howItLoads: The server reads ONE JSON config file, checked in this order: the file at $COPILOT_MCP_CONFIG; else copilot-mcp.config.json in the server's working directory (falling back to the older config.local.json name if that's what exists); else the legacy split files in $COPILOT_MCP_LOCAL_DIR (order-copy-credentials.json + uipath-config.json).

The config is live: every tool call cheaply checks the file's mtime and re-reads + re-validates it when it changed, so editing the file takes effect on the next call — no server restart needed, ever, not just before the first successful load. The server sends an MCP logging notification (notifications/message) each time it picks up a change.

Validation errors name the exact field and path; a missing file lists all three lookup options. If an already-loaded config is edited into something invalid, calls fail with that same validation error (fail closed) rather than silently keeping the old values.

The server is launched through npx (`npx -y @belal-elsabbagh-apex/copilot-mcp`): a small Node launcher that execs the bundled native Go binary for the host platform, so no Node/Bun code runs in the server itself. The launcher passes its whole environment through, so COPILOT_MCP_CONFIG, COPILOT_MCP_CACHE, XDG_CACHE_HOME and the APEX_* variables set in the MCP host's `env` block reach the server.
steps: 1. Ask the user for the values marked <ASK-USER> below — credentials and tokens cannot be guessed and must never be invented.
2. Write the JSON file (template below) somewhere private and gitignored, e.g. ~/.config/copilot-mcp/config.json or copilot-mcp.config.json next to the server.
3. If not using the default copilot-mcp.config.json location, set COPILOT_MCP_CONFIG to the file's absolute path in the MCP host's server config (the `env` block of this server's entry).

4. For any env using support accounts, call the list_clinics tool (env=prod|pre_prod) to get the clinicUid of each clinic and fill copilot.profiles.<name>.<env>.clinicUid; then call the doctor tool (profile=<one of copilot.profiles>) to verify auth + clinic scope + UiPath + Apex.

5. Apex is optional: add the `apex` block (or export APEX_API_URL / APEX_USER_NAME / APEX_PASSWORD) only if you need orchestrator=apex. With neither configured, every orchestrator=apex call fails with 'Apex is not configured' while UiPath and Copilot tools keep working.

uipath.bearer: <ASK-USER: UiPath PAT with OR.Jobs/OR.Queues read scope> (optional if oauth is set)

oauth.clientId: <ASK-USER: UiPath external application client id> (optional block; alternative/fallback pair to bearer)

apex.apiUrl: https://orchestrator.apexmedicalai.com (the load-balancer host, never a CloudFront host) (optional if $APEX_API_URL is set)
apex.username: <ASK-USER: the user's own Apex login — Apex audits writes per user> (optional if $APEX_USER_NAME is set)
apex.password: <ASK-USER: that user's Apex password> (optional if $APEX_PASSWORD is set)
apex.queueUrl: <ASK-USER: the SQS queue URL carried by BE-built Apex items (specific_content.queueUrl)>

fields.copilot.profiles: Named credential sets ('profiles') — every Copilot tool takes a required `profile` arg that must match a key here. Each env of a profile is EITHER a clinicUid pointer (support-account auth: credentials come from copilot.support[env]) OR a full be/email/password login (the per-account shape). clinicUid wins if both are present, which is how one env is migrated without deleting the old credentials.
fields.copilot.support: Support-account credentials per env ({be, email, password, fe?}). Required only for envs whose profiles use clinicUid — today that is prod; pre-prod still uses per-account logins.
fields.copilot.sessionCache: Optional (default true): the single 'anything on disk' switch. true = persist authenticated Copilot sessions (sessions.json) so a restart doesn't spend a login against the support account's 10-logins-per-15-minutes budget, AND persist the Apex JWT / UiPath OAuth token (tokens/) and the terminal-job read caches (cache/<namespace>/: Apex artifact listings + parsed job.log, UiPath RobotLogs + terminal job detail) so a restart does not refetch settled jobs. All under the cache dir (see rules). false = nothing is written to disk, memory only.
fields.copilot.prod / copilot.pre_prod: Optional top-level fallback creds used only when a caller could pass no profile; profiles are the normal path.
fields.uipath.bearer: Single global UiPath PAT/token; UiPath tools take env but no profile. Optional if uipath.oauth is set — still used as the runtime fallback if the OAuth token request fails, so it's fine (and recommended) to keep both configured.
fields.uipath.oauth: Optional: OAuth client-credentials alternative to bearer. Tried first when present; requires clientId + clientSecret. At least one of bearer/oauth is required.
fields.uipath.oauth.tokenUrl: Identity-server token endpoint. Optional — defaults to https://cloud.uipath.com/{org}/identity_/connect/token derived from orchestratorUrl; set explicitly if that guess is wrong (e.g. non-standard/on-prem identity server).
fields.uipath.oauth.scope: Optional OAuth scope string (e.g. 'OR.Jobs OR.Queues OR.Execution').
fields.uipath.folderPathByEnv: Folder per env; defaults exist for the Authorization folders if omitted.
fields.uipath.folderIdByEnv: Optional numeric OrganizationUnitId per env (defaults: prod 231517 / pre_prod 434039).
fields.uipath.queueUrl / uipath.addQueueItemPat: Only needed for build_queue_item / add_queue_item; the safety guard pins posted items to these pre-prod values.
fields.apex: Optional block enabling orchestrator=apex (the Apex orchestrator replacing UiPath portal by portal). Any of apiUrl / username / password the file leaves out is read from APEX_API_URL / APEX_USER_NAME / APEX_PASSWORD (file wins per field). The env fallback only works when the MCP host passes its environment through (CLI hosts and npx do); MCPB installs only pass COPILOT_MCP_CONFIG, so they MUST put Apex in the file. Numbered APEX_API_URL_<n> and APEX_URL are not read. No source configured = Apex calls fail with 'Apex is not configured'; UiPath/Copilot are unaffected.
fields.apex.apiUrl: Apex orchestrator base URL. Use the LB host (https://orchestrator.apexmedicalai.com), NEVER a CloudFront host — CloudFront caps request bodies at 8 KB, which truncates queue-item and job writes.
fields.apex.username / apex.password: The user's OWN Apex login (Apex audits writes per user — no shared bot account). The session JWT (24 h) is reused across restarts via the on-disk token cache (tokens/, mode 0600, keyed by a hash of apiUrl + username) unless copilot.sessionCache is false; the password itself is never written to disk.
fields.apex.folderByEnv: Folder NAME per env; optional, defaults prod='Authorization', pre_prod='Authorization Test'. Names resolve to folder UUIDs at runtime (cached in memory for the process, never persisted) — never put ids here. Every Apex request is scoped by X-Folder-Id; a tool's `folder` arg overrides it for READS only.
fields.apex.serverUrlByEnv / apex.queueUrl: Write guard limits, needed for build_queue_item / add_queue_item on Apex: specific_content.serverURL must equal serverUrlByEnv.pre_prod and a non-empty specific_content.queueUrl must equal queueUrl. Unset = writes are refused (fails closed). Deliberately duplicated with the uipath keys; deleted together with UiPath at retirement.
fields.feedback: Optional on-failure GitHub-issue feedback; on by default (feedback.enabled=false disables). When a tool fails in a way that looks like a bug in this server, the error payload carries reportIssue.url — a prefilled GitHub new-issue link (tool name + error + server version only, no args/credentials) targeting feedback.repositoryUrl (default: this server's repo). Surface or open it so bugs get reported.

rules: NEVER invent credentials, tokens, or emails — every <ASK-USER> value must come from the user.
The config holds secrets: keep it out of version control and never echo passwords/bearer back in chat or logs.
Prod creds grant READ access paths only in practice here: this server's write tools are hard-wired to pre-prod / the dev clone and refuse prod at both the schema and domain layer.
Apex credentials are the operator's own login: never reuse another person's, never echo them, and never point apex.apiUrl at a CloudFront host.

Everything this server writes to disk lives under one cache dir: the directory of $COPILOT_MCP_CACHE if set (that variable names the sessions file; default <cache dir>/sessions.json), else $XDG_CACHE_HOME/copilot-mcp (only when absolute), else ~/.cache/copilot-mcp. Inside: sessions.json (live Copilot JWTs), tokens/ (Apex JWT, UiPath OAuth token), cache/<namespace>/ (job logs and outputs — PHI at rest). Directories are mode 0700, files 0600, file names are key hashes, and the Copilot account email is never stored. Never commit this directory, never echo its contents, and set copilot.sessionCache:false to stop all of it. The cache-consulting read tools (get_job, get_job_logs, build_faulted_job_issue, get_job_artifacts) take `refresh:true` to bypass it when a cached terminal job looks stale.
